title: Russia Bombards 9 Ukrainian Cities Overnight, Killing 2 and Wounding 14+; Kyiv, Odesa, Zaporizhzhia Hit
detail: Russia launched an hours-long aerial barrage overnight into August 27, striking nine Ukrainian cities including Kyiv, Odesa, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Poltava, and Kryvyi Rih with a mix of Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles, an Oniks anti-ship missile, S8000 Banderol cruise missiles, and Shahed-type strike drones. Ukraine's Air Force said it shot down or suppressed 1 Oniks, 7 ballistic missiles, 3 Banderol missiles, and 222 drones. Explosions began around 3:20 a.m. in Kyiv, with debris found in the Podilskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts damaging residential blocks, a school, and a medical facility; no casualties were reported in the capital. A 78-year-old woman was killed in Zaporizhzhia Oblast and another person died in Kharkiv Oblast, with at least 14 people wounded nationwide, including 3 children in Zaporizhzhia. Russia's Defense Ministry called it a 'massive' strike on military-related targets — industrial facilities, oil refineries, logistics hubs, and port infrastructure — while Ukrainian officials said civilian areas including apartment blocks and an educational facility in Odesa were also hit. President Zelensky said 'Russia continues to invest in missiles and in expanding its war, and that means more countermeasures are needed.'

media.caption: Aftermath of Russia's overnight ballistic missile and drone barrage on Kyiv, Aug. 27

title: Russian Drone Kills 1, Injures 5 at Epicentr Shopping Mall in Kharkiv
detail: A Russian jet-powered drone struck an Epicentr hypermarket in Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district on the afternoon of August 27, killing a 40-year-old man and injuring five other people. The strike caused partial structural damage to the building and ignited a fire covering more than 300 square meters. Preliminary data indicated Russian forces used a Geran-4 'Seeker'-type drone.

title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Army Command Posts in Occupied Donetsk with Cruise Missiles
detail: Ukraine's Armed Forces General Staff confirmed a missile strike on the main and reserve command posts of Russian forces near temporarily occupied Donetsk, launched on August 26 and confirmed overnight into August 27. Cruise missiles struck an underground parking area of an unfinished residential complex — reportedly hit by six missiles, per OSINT analysts CyberBoroshno — and the buildings of the former UkrStateNDIplastmas research institute. Ukrainian OSINT group Exilenova+ assessed that a command post of Russia's 51st Guards Combined Arms Army may have been located at one of the affected sites.
